runs.title: Who is the new James Bond, and what's the project?
runs.prompt: Today, October 14, 2026, a new James Bond was officially unveiled. Collider published a story titled 'A New James Bond Has Officially Been Unveiled' about actor Isaac Rouse being revealed at Eton College for a 'Young Bond: SilverFin' audio adaptation. Start with the Collider article and, if you cannot read it, try the publisher Big Finish's site.
runs.answer: The new James Bond is actor Isaac Rouse, unveiled in costume at Eton College as the teenage Bond. The project is not a film or TV series but a full-cast audio drama: "Young Bond: SilverFin," an adaptation of Charlie Higson's first Young Bond novel, told in 16 half-hour episodes (~8 hours) and issued as two box sets (Volumes 1 and 2). It's produced by Big Finish Productions (with the novel by Charlie Higson); Barnaby Edwards is writer/director, Robert Valentine and Lizzie Worsdell are producers, and the cast includes Isaac Rouse plus William Hope, Miriam Margolyes, Paterson Joseph, Tim McInnerny and Miranda Raison. Release date: 29 October 2026 (digital first, then a collector's edition CD), available from bigfinish.com and ianflemingshop.com.

runs.title: Six Kings Slam: why postponed and the new dates?
runs.prompt: The Six Kings Slam tennis exhibition in Riyadh, featuring Carlos Alcaraz, Novak Djokovic and Alexander Zverev, was postponed today, October 14, 2026, after deadly attacks on Saudi Arabia. Find out: why exactly was it postponed, what attacks prompted it, and what are the rescheduled dates? Use the BBC Sport article as your starting point.
runs.answer: The Six Kings Slam in Riyadh was postponed after Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi movement launched a series of deadly attacks on Saudi Arabia, including a missile strike on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport on Saturday that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300, with the kingdom's oil and gas facilities also targeted. Organisers told BBC Sport the decision reflected Riyadh Season's commitment to high standards, following an assessment of the organisational and logistical challenges of hosting the tournament and their potential impact on the quality of the audience experience. The exhibition, which had been set to start on 21 October, has been postponed until 27-30 December.

runs.title: Michelle Parker case: what did Orlando police announce?
runs.prompt: Orlando police announced an arrest today, October 14, 2026, in the long-running missing-person case of Michelle Parker, who disappeared in 2011. Her ex-fiancé Dale Smith was reportedly arrested on second-degree murder charges. Find out from news reports: what charges were announced, who was arrested, and what have police said? Keep it factual and respectful. Start with the Fox 35 Orlando story and the ClickOrlando update.
runs.answer: Orlando police announced Wednesday, Oct. 14, 2026, that Dale Smith Jr., the ex-fiancé of missing Orlando mother Michelle Parker, was arrested on a charge of second-degree murder in her presumed death, nearly 15 years after she disappeared on Nov. 17, 2011. Orlando Police Chief Eric Smith said the arrest came after the department expanded its investigative team over the past year and took a "fresh, focused look at all of the evidence," reexamining testimony and conflicting statements made by the suspect and using advances in digital forensics (including more detailed location data and communications between devices) to uncover and analyze additional evidence. The chief said Smith was arrested at his place of work Wednesday morning and was surprised; Smith had long been considered a suspect but had never before been arrested or charged. Parker, then 33 and a mother of three, was last seen dropping her children off at Smith's home the same day an episode of "The People's Court" aired featuring the two in a dispute over a $5,000 engagement ring.
